Combined adversary: legacy two-part go1.21.json plus an exact diff. Neither is a base candidate for get(): the filename is 'go%s.json' via GoVer.toString() = '1.21.0' (GoApiSnapshot.java:170, GoVer.java:155-158); getApiFile's 'go%d.%d.json' retry (:183-190) is legacy external API, not the get path.

Name-shape attacks on the diff slot: missing '.diff' suffix, trailing '.diff.bak', and a correctly-named diff placed at root instead of under patchverdiffs/. Java only probes 'patchverdiffs/go<M.m.p>.json.diff' (:151) and the model only scans that subdir; all three decoys must be ignored. Base still absent -> missing_base regardless.

Foreign-minor diff (1.22.x) and a noncanonical leading-zero patch name ('03', which GoVer.toString can never produce, GoVer.java:155-158) sit in patchverdiffs/. Base check runs first and fails, so both are unreachable anyway -> missing_base with selected_diff null.

Request patch > 0 pins the base to withPatch(0) -> 'go1.21.0.json' (GoApiSnapshot.java:122). The legacy 'go1.21.json' must not serve as the base even though it would be getApiFile's patch-0 fallback (:186-190); that fallback is outside the get() path by contract.

Degenerate single-component 'go1.json': no filename form in either getApiSnapshotFile (:170) or getApiFile (:185-190) produces it; the shortest possible base name is the two-part getApiFile fallback 'go1.21.json'. Pure noise -> missing_base.

raw_b64 materialization support exercised on the diff slot (b'\xff\x00binary-diff'): opaque non-UTF8 bytes are still just an unreachable diff while the base is absent. Asserts diff bytes are never inspected on the missing_base path.

Missing-base under a non-unix GOOS: 'windows' is outside IS_GOOS_UNIX (:180-181) so the 'unix' slot is '' and dropped; emitted order has four entries. A lower diff is present but unreachable; the reported search order is purely informational on this path.

Legacy go1.21.json carries buckets ('windows', 'bogus-os') that the true base lacks; if the legacy file leaked into bucket matching they would appear (windows matches the search slot pattern only under goos=windows; bogus-os never). Buckets must come solely from go1.21.0.json -> ['all'].

A corrupt legacy file must not poison the run: the get() path never opens go1.21.json, so unparseable bytes there are irrelevant. If the implementation probed the two-part name, _top_level_keys would raise UnreadableError. Expect clean base_only.

Adversarial inode type: 'patchverdiffs' exists but is a regular file. iterdir raises NotADirectoryError (OSError) -> treated as empty -> base_only. Java-equivalent: getApiSnapshotFile('patchverdiffs/go1.21.2.json.diff') finds nothing under a file -> null -> unpatched base (:128-131). Consistent.

Correctly-named diff one level deeper: Java probes exactly 'patchverdiffs/go1.21.3.json.diff' (:151) so a nested copy is invisible; the model's flat iterdir sees only the 'nested' entry whose name fails _DIFF_NAME_RE. base_only, selected_diff null.

Requested patch 0: Java's while loop condition patchVer.getPatch() > 0 (:151-152) never iterates -> no diff probe at all, regardless of later diffs on disk. selected_diff must be null and selected_patch 0 (base bytes), not 7.

Diffs rescue neither absence nor unparseability of the base: with base present-but-corrupt the Java path fails when read() parses the derived stream (:205-240 -> IOException); the model raises UnreadableError from _top_level_keys even though an exact diff was selected. Error, not missing_base and not exact_diff.

Zero-byte base file: exists, so not missing_base; json.load raises JSONDecodeError -> UnreadableError. Distinct decode-failure shape from 'unreadable-base-not-json' (garbage vs empty); Java's JsonReader.peek on EOF likewise fails beginObject (:215).

Support-case: {'raw': str} materialization also carries VALID JSON; bucket order pins search-order position (linux before all), exercising raw-string support on the base slot rather than only the corrupt-diff slot.

Degenerate goos==goarch: Java List.of PERMITS duplicate elements (verified on JDK 21; only Set.of/Map.of reject dupes) so the source order keeps both 'mips' entries (:108-109); only the non-unix '' slot is filtered (read() isEmpty skip :230). Model order must retain duplicates verbatim while bucket matching dedups like LinkedHashMap (:228-237).

goarch='all' collides with the trailing 'all' slot: List.of keeps both ('all','all'), so the emitted order repeats 'all' while base_matching_buckets dedups to ['all']. Pins that arch_search_order is the raw List.of order, not a Set.
